newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines raises interest rates to 24 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines raises interest rates to 24 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank on Wednesday raised its one-day reverse repo rate for the second time in the day and pledged to increase rates again if necessary to defend the peso.
The one-day reverse repo rate was boosted to 24 percent from 20 percent set earlier in the morning following Wednesday's effective devaluation of the Thai baht.
The last time the Bank offered a one-day reverse repo was on June 19 at 15 percent.
The rate usually serves as a benchmark for the Central Bank's closely watched overnight borrowing rate a day later.
"We'll not hesitate to increase it (interest rates) some more if necessary," Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson told Reuters Financial Television.
"We'll act as the market warrants. We cannot anticipate the market," Singson said when questioned if the Bank would intervene further in the currency market.
Earlier in the morning the Bank was a heavy seller of dollars.
Asked if he expected rates to stay high, Singson said: "I hope not for very long because the fundamentals are very good."

He reiterated that Manila was determined to defend the peso from what it considers to be a speculative attack spilling over from the slump in the Thai baht following the introduction of a managed float.
If the Bank was convinced this was not a speculative attack it would not intervene, he added.
Singson ruled out any introduction of capital controls or a two-tier currency system.
